posts.note: Fiction piece (a dying character, John DiNapoli) not logged: no sincere real-world claim. One newsletter-programming promise in the preamble.
Satirical Apple Vision Pro review and fake 'Delete You' app pitch; two sincere-reading product remarks logged.
Announcement of a psychedelic review series for primary care; one dated publication call.
Satirical vampire lawsuit against LifeStance built on the Hindenburg short report. One implicit own call, one quoted Hindenburg forecast. Fake complaint text itself not logged.
Pointer to Bess Stillman's essay plus a personal open letter; nothing forward-looking.
500th post on the J&J ERISA class action; dense with explicit predictions about ERISA enforcement, PBMs, self-funded plans and validated vendors.
Drug review and forest-plot tutorial; no forward-looking claims.
Guest article by Sharena Rice, Ph.D., in dialogue format. Three hedged biomarker forecasts, all in the guest's words (own_claim false).
Podcast blurb plus Spring Health validation news; only normative 'employers need to' language.
Podcast blurb on the Nature Medicine ibogaine study; one vague 'healing is coming' line.
Music-streaming economics essay; four low-relevance forward-looking claims about Spotify payouts and recorded music.

Scam-conference essay; only a trivial Spatial Video promise.

statements.quote: If you're looking for some awesome review of the evidence, stay tuned for tomorrow. I'm sure they'll be more of that coming!
statements.context: Preamble to a fiction piece. The author says the newsletter will return to evidence reviews the next day and that more such reviews are coming. Concerns the author's own newsletter output (post dated 2024-02-02).
statements.note: Own-newsletter programming promise; low forecast value. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: This will make it not a productivity tool unless you are in the “neck workout set.”
statements.context: After a hands-on in-store demo of the Apple Vision Pro (heavy on the face after 30 minutes, neck strain), the author claims the headset will not become a productivity tool. The post is a self-described satirical weekend piece, but this line reads as a sincere product assessment ('Everything other reviewers say is true').
statements.note: Satirical post, sincere-reading product call about Vision Pro adoption as a productivity device.

statements.quote: Few 8-year-olds will drop $3500 on this…but what do I know?
statements.context: Joke about the 13-year age limit for the in-store Apple Vision Pro demo and the author's son (not yet 8). Trivial market observation that children will not buy the $3,500 device.
statements.note: Joke framing; trivially true market remark. Logged for recall only.

statements.quote: Along with friends, I helped get this series out the door, which will be published with peer review in March 2024.
statements.context: An eight-part review series on psychedelic medicine (introduction, LSD, DMT and ayahuasca, psilocybin, ibogaine, MDMA, ketamine, SWOT conclusion) written for primary care physicians and general medical doctors. The author says peer-reviewed publication is due in March 2024 (post dated 2024-02-04).
statements.note: Own-work publication timing; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: now the “putting Vampires to Shame” Private Equity Guys at LastChoice BloodCare Partners have decided to feast on the not yet completely dead and bloated corpse of Lifestance
statements.context: Satirical intro to a fake vampire lawsuit. Real setup: Hindenburg Research published a short report on LifeStance Health, the share price fell 72% since the NASDAQ listing, and investor class actions were filed. Calling LifeStance a 'not yet completely dead' corpse implies the author expects the company to fail.
statements.note: Implicit call inside satire; the author also calls the listing a 'pump-and-dump'. The fake complaint text is not logged.

statements.quote: Overall, we think LifeStance is a classic example of what happens when private equity meets a ‘hot’ healthcare sector: Massive debt fueling a grinding, metric-focused corporate culture resulting in worse quality of care for patients, a worse environment for clinicians and long-term losses for the average investor.
statements.context: Bullet quoted from the Hindenburg Research short report on LifeStance Health, reproduced inside the satirical complaint with the author's annotations. Hindenburg expects long-term losses for LifeStance investors.
statements.note: Third-party (Hindenburg) forecast quoted by the author, who appears sympathetic but does not restate it in his own words.

statements.quote: This is the real gravamen 4 of this case (and the thousands of others coming): no prudent person would agree to this nonsense.
statements.context: 500th post. A class action alleges Johnson & Johnson's Pension & Benefits Committee breached ERISA fiduciary duty by letting its PBM charge $10,239.69 for a generic drug available for about $40. The author says thousands of similar ERISA fiduciary cases are coming. '4' is a footnote marker defining 'gravamen'.
statements.note: Quantified expectation of follow-on ERISA fiduciary litigation ('thousands').

statements.quote: I have argued that the “PBM part” of the ERISA fiduciary breach claims is just the beginning.
statements.context: Under the heading 'I made great predictions.' The J&J case is about PBM drug pricing; the author expects ERISA fiduciary-breach claims to expand beyond PBM costs to the whole health plan ('The entire health plan needs not be a scam').
statements.note: Restates an earlier call from the author's ERISA articles.

statements.quote: The next enforcement, I predict, will focus on prior authorization and its role in strategically blocking cost-effective care to increase the plant administrator's profits at the expense of the plan member.
statements.context: Explicit prediction of the next wave of ERISA fiduciary enforcement after the J&J PBM case: prior authorization practices of plan administrators. 'plant administrator' is the author's typo for plan administrator.
statements.note: Direct, self-labelled prediction.

statements.quote: Behavioral health is the lowest-hanging fruit regarding enforcement around access because the regulations are the most stringent.
statements.context: Follows the prior-authorization prediction. The author argues enforcement over access to care will hit behavioral health first, citing the ten-day appointment access rule under the ACA built on ERISA and the shortage of psychiatric experts.
statements.note: Present-tense assessment with a predictive reading: behavioral health access will be an early enforcement target.

statements.quote: This also means there are a ton of lawsuits in the making against plan administrators by employers asking them to provide the data to demonstrate that they are behaving appropriately.
statements.context: Item 'Get Your Data' in the author's list of next steps for employers after the J&J ERISA case. He expects many employer-versus-plan-administrator lawsuits over access to claims data.
statements.note: Litigation-volume call about employers suing plan administrators for data.

statements.quote: I predict there will be a stampede towards self-funded plans
statements.context: Item 'Go Self-Funded' in the next-steps list. The author predicts employers will move en masse to self-funded health plans because fiduciary liability under fully insured plans is too high.
statements.note: Compound sentence; the second half (implosion of fully funded plans) is logged separately.

statements.quote: we may see in the next year or two the complete implosion of fully funded plans sponsored by employers—the liability is just too high.
statements.context: Second half of the 'Go Self-Funded' item: the author says fully funded (fully insured) employer-sponsored health plans may collapse completely within one to two years of the post (dated 2024-02-07).
statements.horizon_text: in the next year or two
statements.note: Dated, hedged call; companion to the self-funded stampede statement.

statements.quote: PBM lawsuits will be relatively easy with this precedent, so there will be many more of those
statements.context: Item 'Get a New PBM'. With the J&J complaint as precedent, the author expects many more lawsuits over pharmacy benefit manager pricing.
statements.note: Litigation-volume call about PBM suits.

statements.quote: essentially every company using anything other than cost-plus drugs , Capital RX , or one of the other cost-plus PBM vendors. Dead in the water in the employer market.
statements.context: Continuation of 'Get a New PBM': the author says traditional (non-cost-plus) PBMs are finished in the employer market, and any employer not using Cost Plus Drugs, Capital Rx or another cost-plus PBM is exposed to suit.
statements.note: Spacing before the commas is in the source text. Market-shift call about traditional PBMs.

statements.quote: Validated solutions for cost savings that offer plausible deniability or actual fulfillment of fiduciary duty will become popular.
statements.context: Item 'Buy Validated Solutions'. The author expects independently validated cost-saving vendors (he cites the Validation Institute) to gain popularity with employers as fiduciary pressure grows. He discloses that one of his own jobs sells a validated mental health solution with a $1 million D&O indemnification.
statements.note: Author has a disclosed interest (a validated mental health vendor, likely Acacia Clinics).

statements.quote: employers have to stop getting scammed, or they will be held personally responsible, and nobody wants that for themselves.
statements.context: Closing paragraph. Conditional: if employers do not stop overpaying for health benefits and pharmacy costs, their named fiduciaries will be held personally liable under ERISA.
statements.note: Exhortation with a predictive consequence clause.

statements.quote: Now we know who those people will be in the subsequent lawsuits at your company
statements.context: Footnote 2, attached to the explanation that health benefits are tax-exempt because a fiduciary agrees to act in members' interest. The author expects subsequent ERISA lawsuits at other companies to name benefits-committee members personally, as the J&J complaint did.
statements.note: Footnote text.

statements.quote: More biomarkers may emerge with advances in machine learning, computing, materials science, biosensing, and clinical trials.
statements.context: Guest article by neuroscientist Sharena Rice, Ph.D., in dialogue with the author. Answering Owen's question 'How will more biomarkers change this sort of research…is more coming?', she says more mental-health biomarkers may emerge from advances in machine learning, computing, materials science, biosensing and clinical trials.
statements.note: Guest co-author's statement in reply to the author's question; the author does not restate it.

statements.quote: Over time, we may discover more types of objective biomarkers using combinations of sensors and less invasive techniques to give more people access to how their minds are doing.
statements.context: Sharena Rice, after reviewing EEG, fMRI, TD-fNIRS and implant-based biomarkers (Mount Sinai DBS depression biomarkers, Kernel headset). She expects more objective, less invasive mental-health biomarkers over time.
statements.note: Guest co-author's statement.

statements.quote: Design advances have the potential to provide biosensor systems better integration into people’s lives outside of the clinic or research lab!
statements.context: Sharena Rice on wearable biosensor systems moving out of the clinic and research lab into daily life.
statements.note: Weak, capability-style claim by the guest co-author; logged for recall.

statements.quote: Please spread the good word—healing is coming, and more evidence is needed to understand when and for whom
statements.context: Podcast post on the Cherian et al. Nature Medicine study of magnesium-ibogaine in veterans with TBI and PTSD, discussed with Jeremy Fox. The author closes with a general expectation that psychedelic treatments such as ibogaine will bring healing, while noting the evidence gap.
statements.note: Vague, aspirational call; no specific event or date.

statements.quote: Working as a “recording” artist is not financially viable. Which means, for all of us, less great recorded music.
statements.context: Essay on streaming economics written after the author released his own music. He argues streaming royalties make recording unviable and predicts the result will be less great recorded music.
statements.note: Economic consequence claim outside health; low relevance.

statements.quote: Those negligible payouts will now be re-allocated to the total pool paid out to musicians directly we have greater than 1000 streams.
statements.context: Describes Spotify's announced royalty change: songs with between 1 and 1,000 streams will get no payout ('the payout will now be … nothing') and that money will be re-allocated to artists with more than 1,000 streams. 'directly we have' is the author's typo for 'who have'.
statements.note: Restates Spotify's announced policy rather than an independent forecast.

statements.quote: My total revenue from being on Spotify will now go to zero!
statements.context: Consequence of the Spotify policy change for the author's own small catalogue: his streaming revenue will fall to zero.
statements.note: Trivial personal forecast; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Other more rational people will not make the same decisions, however.
statements.context: The author says he can afford to record on expensive equipment he will never recoup because he has another job; he expects other, more rational musicians will not keep making such investments under streaming economics.
statements.note: General behavioral claim about musicians; weak.

statements.quote: In the near future, fMRI-guided neuromodulation treatment, robust walking , and other novel interventions will be the standard of care.
statements.context: Personal essay on bipolar disorder and residency accommodations. The author, now treated with TMS, predicts fMRI-guided neuromodulation (the approach his Acacia Clinics uses), 'robust walking' and other novel interventions will become the standard of care for mood disorders.
statements.note: Author's own clinic sells fMRI-guided TMS; coder may mark CONTROL. Spacing before the comma is in the source.

statements.quote: Well, I suspect this is going to bite The Lord of Defamation really hard…and here is how
statements.context: Legal/math post on New York civil judgments against Donald Trump (9% statutory interest, escrow required for appeals, about $450M civil fraud judgment in the case brought by AG Letitia James). 'This' is the Carroll v. Trump II precedent that a second defamation of an adjudicated matter skips liability and goes straight to damages. The author expects it to cost Trump heavily.
statements.note: Legal-financial forecast outside health.

statements.quote: Thus, if AG James were to want to really Dunk on the D, she, and even Judge Engoron would be well within their rights to sue him for defamation. They would, as established, auto-win
statements.context: Conditional: if AG Letitia James or Judge Engoron sued Trump for calling them 'Crooked' and 'Corrupt' after the fraud verdict, the author says they would automatically win on liability under the Carroll II precedent and proceed to damages. Footnote 1 hedges: 'This is a plausible outcome, but not a certain one.'
statements.note: Conditional legal call; the author's own footnote downgrades it to plausible, not certain.

statements.quote: What happens when saying false and defamatory things (previously adjudicated) becomes a more expensive hobby—in a state court, not federal—than anyone can possibly afford? We may be about to find out.
statements.context: Closing lines. The author suggests Trump's continued statements about adjudicated matters may soon produce unaffordable defamation liability in New York state court.
statements.note: Rhetorical question followed by a hedged expectation.

statements.quote: My real point is that in NYS, adjudicated defamation by serial defamers creates a nasty financial bind. They won’t stop/can’t stop, but interest accrues on the behavior.
statements.context: Footnote 1. The author predicts serial defamers (Trump) will not stop making adjudicated-false statements while 9% interest accrues on the resulting New York judgments.
statements.note: Footnote; behavioral prediction about Trump.

statements.quote: That will be a Spatial Video soon.
statements.context: Opening aside while on vacation: a poolside photo will become a Spatial Video (Apple Vision Pro format) soon. Concerns the author's own content.
statements.note: Trivial own-content promise; coder may mark CONTROL. The rest of the post (scam conferences, Elsevier) has no forward-looking claims.
